head: 661bc6733

boundaries: the send request and the uploaded bytes
the recipient key the server publishes

notes: Cleanups asked for by the user. The CI failure on cf1edd9dc (a test outside src expecting the old avatar path) was fixed before this review opened, in 428908bc5; H3 now says to search frontend/tests too.

instruments.evidence: Review of the four cleanups on top of cf1edd9dc: one recipient-key lookup (recipientKeys.ts, 4275b3afc), group drag and drop through one sealing rule (fileSealing.ts, cde5cea8f), New Message in an empty messages column (e3ad9feb0), the gitleaks test-vector exception (4b18b2ef6), and the CI fix for the avatar path test (428908bc5). Boundaries: the send request and the uploaded bytes; the key the server publishes; the rendered column; the gitleaks scan.

Read d66091636 (the review these cleanups came out of: its E5 note named the three inline copies, and its pass-2 UX notes named the drop-into-group refusal and the empty column) and d2697f1f3, whose feed-column control this review touches.

Printed the requests that leave the device for two conversation kinds each: a drop into a group (one sealed envelope, group_key_version, no sender copy) and into a direct message (caption as content, both key copies, each opening the uploaded bytes); the expanded view into a group (text as content) and a direct message (the file sealed for both readers with the key getPublicKeys returned).
The empty messages column, rendered: New Message above the inbox's own empty state ('No messages yet'); a non-messages column still renders its bare empty state.
Read in B5: upload 201, send 423 then 201, the stored message body.
The stored message read back in B5: encryption_version v2, caption v2 ciphertext, media_type image/png, both key copies, 308 bytes for a 292-byte PNG.

One refusal code for every missing or unreadable recipient key ('recipient-key-unusable'), mapped once by messageSendErrorKey; the gitleaks path pattern matches the paths gitleaks reports (repository-relative, as the scans show).

The drop path read user1_id/user2_id while every other sender read other_user; the server sends both for a direct message (ConversationWithDetails). Changed to other_user in 661bc6733 so there is one way to find a recipient.
Two sealing rules existed (the composer's and drag and drop's); both now call sealFileForConversation. The DM branch that the feed column wrote out by hand became the same call.
gitleaks-action loads .gitleaks.toml from the repository root; verified locally with the same rules: full-history git scans with and without the file differ by exactly the vector findings.

instruments.why: No field added to anything that crosses a boundary.

instruments.evidence: The page and column tests' fixtures now carry other_user as the server sends it; the new DM drop case failed on the old fixture only because the drop path read a field the fixture lacked -- which is what C2 changed.
Real inputs: a PNG dropped into a direct message (real browser) and into a group (test), a message typed into an expanded group and direct conversation.

Hostile inputs still refused: no own keys, a recipient that publishes no key or an unreadable one (both 'recipient-key-unusable'), a group member not set up. The same test-vector content copied outside shared/crypto-vectors is still caught by gitleaks.
An empty inbox is the boundary for the column; a conversation with no other_user (group, mod mail) for the senders.
Siblings of the drop path: the composer, the feed column's New Message box, the expanded view. The expanded view is the finding below.
All branches reachable: sealFileForConversation group / DM / refusals.
Every refusal reaches the person: the drop and expanded paths alert through messageSendErrorKey; the expanded view's upload failure now names its refusal instead of a generic upload failure.

Conditions on conversation_type re-read in every sender; mod mail has its own multi-recipient path on the page, and the expanded view now refuses it through the service with a reason (before, it refused with "recipient not found").

Found and removed: five copies of the recipient-key lookup, two of the sealing rule, a second rule for finding the recipient (C2). The multi-person forward keeps its batch lookup: a different shape, one request for many users.

The shape 'a sender looks for a single recipient, so groups stop at recipient not found' was searched in every send path. It is also in the feed column's expanded view: the column lists groups and expands them, and every send stopped. Finding below. Voice looks for no recipient (it is still unencrypted: G4b).
A refusal happens before any upload, so nothing is left behind.

One finding, one control: expanded-view-refused-groups. With the view restored, all three new tests fail with real assertions (nothing is sent for the group; the direct message carries encrypted_content where content is expected). Each fix commit also had its new test run against the old code before committing: the drop test, the empty-column test.
The gitleaks exception is read by the CI job from the root .gitleaks.toml on every push; the scan tested locally with that file.
tsc -b 0; eslint and prettier clean on all 11 changed frontend files; the pre-commit hook passed every commit.
E6 found it; named. One ratchet from this change set, for H3: search frontend/tests as well as src -- the red CI run on cf1edd9dc was a test outside src that the last review never ran.

Ran for real: the dev stack, the signed-in pane, a PNG dropped into the direct message. Upload 201, the send waited out the scan (423, then 201), no alert; the stored row is sealed as B4 says. Not shown for real: a group (the account has none, and the pane's key pair stays unrepaired until the user's next sign-in, so it can open no group key) and the empty column (the account has conversations). Those two are pinned by the page and column tests.
Known-bad input to gitleaks: the same key-shaped content outside the folder is flagged (2 findings); default rules stay on (useDefault).

instruments.why: No bar or row changed width.

instruments.evidence: 134 passed, 1 skipped (the old MessagesPage keyboard it.skip); nothing new skips.

instruments.why: Cleanups the user asked for by name; no plan phase.
Each send is one user action; the drop loop is sequential.

instruments.evidence: Searched src AND tests (the H3 amendment this review made, after tests/unit/editProfileModal.test.tsx turned CI red on cf1edd9dc): 20 test files name a changed module (ColumnFeed, ExpandedMessage, MessagesPage, fileSealing, messagesService, recipientKeys), all pass; all 37 files in tests/unit pass.

Re-applied every control this review and d66091636 own: 12 apply; g4a2b-feed-column-uploaded-the-file-itself (d2697f1f3) was stale after the column moved to sealFileForConversation, and is rebuilt so it still uploads the raw file: 'expected Uint8Array[137, 80, 78, 71, ...] to not deeply equal' the original.

instruments.why: No resource acquired after an await.

instruments.evidence: recipientKeys.ts and fileSealing.ts were made separate modules so the page tests, which mock keyManagementService and messagesService, run them for real on the production functions rather than on a stand-in.

findings.summary: The feed column lists and expands group conversations, but its expanded view looked for a single recipient before sending, so every message into a group -- text or file -- stopped at 'recipient not found'.

control.observed: With the view restored: 3 of 3 fail -- 'expected "vi.fn()" to be called at least once' for both group cases (nothing sent), and the direct-message case sends encrypted_content where content is expected. The test renders the real component; the only earlier test of it replaced it with a stub.
